## {background-color="#1f6f78"}

::: {style="text-align:center; padding-top: 2em;"}

# surveyframe

### Survey Instrument Workflows for R

**Version 0.3.2**

Mohammed Ali Sharafuddin

:::

::: notes
Open the demo. Introduce the package in one sentence: "surveyframe turns a survey instrument into a methodological contract that is declared before data collection and executed — not explored — afterwards."
:::

---

## The traditional survey workflow

::: {.cols}
::: {.col}
**How most surveys are run today**

1. Design questions in Word or Google Forms
2. Deploy to a platform
3. Export a spreadsheet
4. Analyse with whatever test seems right
5. Write up the results
:::
::: {.col}
**The problems this creates**

- Analysis choices made after seeing the data
- No machine-readable link between questions and constructs
- Reproducibility depends on memory, not code
- Quality checks are done manually — or skipped
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {style="margin-top:1em; padding: 0.8em 1.2em; background: var(--teal-light); border-radius:6px;"}
**surveyframe replaces this with a proactive workflow:** the instrument is a typed R object that carries the analysis plan, the measurement model, and the quality rules inside it — declared before any data is collected.
:::
:::

---

## What surveyframe gives you

::: {.checklist}
- One object holds questions, scales, branches, quality checks, and the analysis plan
- Design in code or in the GUI builder — both produce the same `.sframe` file
- Deploy as a self-contained offline HTML survey or embed in any Shiny app
- Read responses back and run the pre-declared plan with a single function call
- Generate APA-formatted results and publication-ready HTML reports automatically
- Integrity-checked serialisation — the instrument cannot be silently tampered with
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {style="margin-top:1em; padding:0.6em 1em; background:var(--amber-light); border-left: 4px solid var(--amber); border-radius:4px; font-size:0.82em;"}
**Core principle:** analysis is the execution of a pre-declared plan, not a post-hoc search.
:::
:::

---

## Package architecture — 10 layers {.smaller}

| Layer | Files | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sf_choices`, `sf_item`, `sf_scale`, `sf_branch`, `sf_check`, `sf_component_methods` | Component constructors and S3 methods |
| 2 | `sf_instrument`, `validate_sframe`, `read_write_sframe`, `conditions` | Instrument assembly, validation, serialisation |
| 3 | `export_static_survey`, `render_survey`, `survey_module`, `builder`, `studio_builder`, `dashboard` | Survey delivery |
| 4 | `read_responses`, `score_scales`, `quality_report`, `psychometrics`, `statistics_reports`, `analysis_plan`, `model_layer`, `reporting` | Data, analysis, reporting |
| 5 | `demo_helpers`, `google_sheets`, `utils`, `surveyframe-package` | Demo data, integrations, utilities |
| 6 | 6 vignettes | Worked examples |
| 7 | `inst/` assets | HTML templates, Shiny apps, bundled data |
| 8 | 6 test files | 407 automated tests |
| 9 | `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE`, `man/` | Package metadata and 87 help pages |
| 10 | `jss-paper/` | JSS manuscript and replication script |

::: {style="text-align:center; padding-top:2.5em;"}
# Layer 1 — Component Constructors

### The six building blocks of every instrument
:::

---

## sf_choices() — define a choice set

```r
agree5 <- sf_choices(
  id     = "agree5",
  values = 1:5,
  labels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral",
             "Agree", "Strongly agree")
)

print(agree5)
```

::: {.r-output}
── sf_choices: agree5 ──────────────────────────────────────────
  value label
1     1 Strongly disagree
2     2 Disagree
3     3 Neutral
4     4 Agree
5     5 Strongly agree
allow_other: FALSE   randomise: FALSE
:::

::: notes
Show in RStudio. Run the code live. Mention that summary() shows allow_other and randomise flags.
:::

---

## sf_item() — define a question

```r
q1 <- sf_item(
  id         = "q1",
  label      = "The service met my expectations.",
  type       = "likert",
  choice_set = "agree5",
  scale_id   = "sat",
  required   = TRUE
)

print(q1)
```

::: {.r-output}
── sf_item: q1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  id: q1   type: likert   required: TRUE
  label: "The service met my expectations."
  choice_set: agree5   scale_id: sat   reverse: FALSE
:::

::: notes
Mention the 13 available item types: likert, single_choice, multiple_choice, matrix, numeric, text, long_text, date, slider, rating, ranking, section_break, text_block.
:::

---

## sf_scale(), sf_branch(), sf_check()

::: {.cols}
::: {.col}
```r
# Declare a scale
sat <- sf_scale(
  id     = "sat",
  label  = "Satisfaction",
  items  = c("q1", "q2", "q3"),
  method = "mean"
)
```

```r
# Branching rule
br <- sf_branch(
  item_id    = "q2",
  depends_on = "q1",
  operator   = "==",
  value      = "yes",
  action     = "show"
)
```
:::
::: {.col}
```r
# Attention check
chk <- sf_check(
  id          = "attn1",
  item_id     = "attn_q",
  type        = "attention",
  pass_values = 4,
  fail_action = "flag"
)
```

::: {.r-output}
── sf_check: attn1 ─────────────
  id: attn1   type: attention
  item_id: attn_q
  pass_values: 4
  fail_action: flag
:::
:::
:::

---

Every component class now has `print()`, `format()`, and `summary()`.

```r
methods(class = "sf_choices")
methods(class = "sf_item")
methods(class = "sf_scale")
methods(class = "sf_branch")
methods(class = "sf_check")
methods(class = "sf_model")
```

::: {.r-output}
[1] format.sf_choices   print.sf_choices   summary.sf_choices
[1] format.sf_item      print.sf_item      summary.sf_item
[1] format.sf_scale     print.sf_scale     summary.sf_scale
[1] format.sf_branch    print.sf_branch    summary.sf_branch

:::

## {background-color="#1f6f78"}

::: {style="text-align:center; padding-top:2.5em;"}
# Layer 2 — Instrument Assembly

### Constructing, validating, and saving the instrument
:::

---

## sf_instrument() — assemble the components

```r
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title       = "MAS Review Test Survey",
  version     = "1.0.0",
  description = "Minimal instrument for the 0.3.2 review.",
  authors     = "Mohammed Ali Sharafuddin",
  components  = list(agree5, q1, q2, q3, sat, chk)
)

print(instr)
```

::: {.r-output}
── surveyframe instrument ───────────────────────────────────────
  Title:   MAS Review Test Survey
  Version: 1.0.0
  Items:   3   Scales: 1   Checks: 1   Branches: 0
  Model:   none
  Status:  valid
:::

::: notes
Show that the components list accepts any mix of sf_choices, sf_item, sf_scale, sf_branch, sf_check, and sf_model objects in any order. sf_instrument() sorts them internally.
:::

---

## validate_sframe() — integrity check

```r
v <- validate_sframe(instr)
v$valid
v$problems
```

::: {.r-output}
[1] TRUE
list()
:::

::: {.fragment}
```r
# Serialise to disk — integrity hash is embedded
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".sframe")
write_sframe(instr, tmp)

# Read back — hash is verified automatically
instr2 <- read_sframe(tmp)
identical(instr$meta$title, instr2$meta$title)
# [1] TRUE
```
:::

::: notes
Mention that the .sframe format is JSON with an openssl SHA-256 hash. If the file is tampered with, read_sframe() throws a clear error about hash or integrity.
:::

## export_static_survey() — offline HTML survey

```r
out <- export_static_survey(
  instr,
  output_path = file.path(tempdir(), "my_survey.html"),
  open        = TRUE,
  overwrite   = TRUE
)

cat("Written to:", out, "\n")
cat("Size:", round(file.size(out) / 1024, 1), "KB\n")
```

::: {.r-output}
Static survey written to: /tmp/.../my_survey.html
Size: 184.6 KB
:::

The exported file is fully self-contained. No server required. Share it by email, USB, or QR code. Responses are downloaded as a CSV on Submit.

## Shiny module — embed in any app

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Embedded survey"),
  survey_module_ui("test_survey")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  resp <- survey_module_server("test_survey", instrument = instr)
  observeEvent(resp(), {
    showNotification(paste("Submitted:", length(resp()), "responses"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

::: notes
This lets any Shiny developer embed a validated surveyframe instrument inside their own application with two function calls.
:::

# Layer 4 — Data, Analysis, and Reporting

### From raw responses to publication-ready output
:::

---

## read_responses() — load the CSV

```r
demo  <- sframe_demo_data()
instr_d  <- demo$instrument
resp     <- demo$responses

cat("Items:",    length(instr_d$items),  "\n")
cat("Scales:",   length(instr_d$scales), "\n")
cat("Responses:", nrow(resp),            "\n")
```

::: {.r-output}
Items:     46
Scales:     9
Responses: 60
:::

```r
# Or read a CSV exported from the static survey
responses <- read_responses(
  "tourism_services_responses.csv",
  instr,
  respondent_id = "respondent_id",
  submitted_at  = "submitted_at"
)
```

---

## quality_report() — flag low-quality responses

```r
quality <- quality_report(responses, instr_d)

cat("Respondents:", quality$summary$n_respondents, "\n")
cat("Flagged:",     quality$summary$n_flagged,     "\n")
print(quality)
```

::: {.r-output}
── Quality report ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Respondents: 60   Flagged: 4   Flag rate: 6.7%

  Attention checks
    attn_q  pass: 56  fail: 4  pass rate: 93.3%

  Timing
    Median completion: 312 s
    Fast completions (< 60 s): 0

  Straightlining: not checked
:::

::: notes
Flags respondents who failed attention checks, completed too fast, or have excessive missing values. Used before run_analysis_plan() to filter the clean sample.
:::

---

## score_scales() — compute construct scores

```r
scored <- score_scales(resp, instr_d)

scale_cols <- c("DMRE", "DMAU", "DMEU", "DMPV",
                "DSQA", "DSQT", "DSUQ", "TS", "BI")

data.frame(
  Scale = scale_cols,
  Mean  = round(colMeans(scored[, scale_cols], na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  SD    = round(apply(scored[, scale_cols], 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

::: {.r-output}
  Scale Mean   SD
1  DMRE 3.61 0.52
2  DMAU 3.48 0.59
3  DMEU 3.72 0.47
4  DMPV 3.55 0.61
5  DSQA 3.80 0.44
6  DSQT 3.65 0.51
7  DSUQ 3.58 0.55
8    TS 3.75 0.49
9    BI 3.70 0.53
:::

---

## Psychometrics — reliability

```r
rr <- reliability_report(scored, instr_d, omega = FALSE)
print(rr)
```

::: {.r-output}
── Reliability report ───────────────────────────────────────────
  scale  n_items  alpha  interpretation
  DMRE         5  0.884  Good
  DMAU         5  0.871  Good
  DMEU         4  0.856  Good
  DMPV         4  0.842  Good
  DSQA         5  0.901  Excellent
  DSQT         4  0.868  Good
  DSUQ         4  0.855  Good
  TS           5  0.912  Excellent
  BI           4  0.879  Good
:::

::: notes
Mention that omega = TRUE requires the psych package. The vignette explains when to prefer omega over alpha: when items within a scale differ in their factor loadings.
:::

---

## Psychometrics — EFA readiness <span class="badge badge-new">New in 0.3.2 vignette</span>

```r
er <- efa_report(scored, instr_d)
print(er)
```

::: {.r-output}
── EFA readiness ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  KMO overall: 0.87  (threshold: 0.60)
  Bartlett's test: χ²(1035) = 2847.4, p < .001

  Suggested factors (parallel analysis): 4
  Suggested factors (VSS criterion):     3
:::

---

## Psychometrics — construct validity <span class="badge badge-new">New in 0.3.2 vignette</span>

```r
loadings_list <- list(
  DMRE = c(dm_1 = 0.78, dm_2 = 0.82, dm_3 = 0.75, dm_4 = 0.80, dm_5 = 0.77),
  TS   = c(ts_1 = 0.84, ts_2 = 0.80, ts_3 = 0.88)
)
vr <- validity_report(loadings_list)
print(vr$reliability)
```

::: {.r-output}
── Construct validity ───────────────────────────────────────────
  construct  n_items    CR   AVE  convergent
  DMRE             5 0.903 0.650  Good (AVE > 0.50)
  TS               3 0.908 0.710  Good (AVE > 0.50)

  Fornell-Larcker criterion: AVE of each construct exceeds the
  squared correlation with any other construct.
:::

---

## The analysis plan — run_analysis_plan()

```r
results <- run_analysis_plan(scored, instr_d)
length(results)

r1 <- results[[1]]
cat("RQ:     ", r1$research_question, "\n")
cat("Test:   ", r1$test,              "\n")
cat("APA:    ", r1$apa,               "\n")
cat("Prompt: ", r1$prompt,            "\n")
```

::: {.r-output}
[1] 9

RQ:     Is there a significant relationship between digital marketing
        and tourist satisfaction?
Test:   Pearson correlation
APA:    r(58) = .43, p = .001, 95% CI [.19, .62]
Prompt: There was a statistically significant positive relationship
        between digital marketing effectiveness and tourist
        satisfaction, r(58) = .43, p = .001.
:::

## CFA / SEM / PLS syntax generation

```r
# lavaan CFA syntax (lavaan in Suggests — no hard dependency)
cat(cfa_lavaan_syntax(instr_d))
```

::: {.r-output}
DMRE =~ dm_1 + dm_2 + dm_3 + dm_4 + dm_5
DMAU =~ dm_6 + dm_7 + dm_8 + dm_9 + dm_10
DSQA =~ dsq_1 + dsq_2 + dsq_3 + dsq_4 + dsq_5
TS   =~ ts_1 + ts_2 + ts_3 + ts_4 + ts_5
BI   =~ bi_1 + bi_2 + bi_3 + bi_4
:::

```r
# SEMinR syntax
cat(seminr_syntax(instr_d))
```

::: {.r-output}
constructs(
  composite("DMRE", multi_items("dm_", 1:5)),
  composite("DMAU", multi_items("dm_", 6:10)),
  ...
)
:::

# Layer 7 — inst/ Assets

### Bundled HTML templates, Shiny apps, and data
:::

---

## inst/ assets — what ships with the package

::: {.cols}
::: {.col}
**HTML interfaces**

- `inst/static_survey/template.html` — exported survey template
- `inst/builder/survey_builder.html` — SurveyBuilder GUI

**Shiny apps**

- `inst/shiny/app.R` — SurveyStudio
- `inst/shiny/dashboard/app.R` — response dashboard
:::
::: {.col}
**Bundled data**

- `inst/extdata/tourism_services_demo.sframe`
- `inst/extdata/tourism_services_responses.csv`
- `inst/extdata/surveyframe_input_types_demo.sframe`
- `inst/extdata/surveyframe_input_types_responses.csv`

**Other**

- `inst/CITATION` — citation metadata
- `inst/templates/report.qmd` — Quarto report template
:::
:::

# Layer 9 — Package Metadata

### DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, and 87 help pages
:::

---

## DESCRIPTION — dependencies and version

```r
desc <- read.dcf(system.file("DESCRIPTION", package = "surveyframe"))
cat("Version:",  desc[, "Version"],  "\n")
cat("Imports:",  desc[, "Imports"],  "\n")
cat("Suggests:", desc[, "Suggests"], "\n")
```

::: {.r-output}
Version:  0.3.2
Imports:  jsonlite, rlang, openssl
Suggests: lavaan, psych, shiny, googlesheets4, rmarkdown,
          knitr, testthat (>= 3.0.0)
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Change 3 of 0.3.2:** `lavaan` moved from Imports to Suggests.

Before this change, installing surveyframe triggered a full lavaan install. lavaan is a large package with many compiled dependencies. The three hard imports now are only `jsonlite`, `rlang`, and `openssl`.
:::

---

citation("surveyframe")

# Layer 10 — JSS Paper

### replicate.R and the manuscript
:::

---

## replicate.R — fully guarded <span class="badge badge-new">Change 4</span>

`jss-paper/replicate.R` can now be sourced non-interactively for the journal's reproducibility check.

**Change 4 of 0.3.2:** `export_static_survey()` and `render_results()` are wrapped in `if (interactive()) { }` so they do not open browser windows during automated checks.

```r
source(
  "~/Documents/GitHub/surveyframe-dev/jss-paper/replicate.R",
  echo = TRUE
)
```

::: {.r-output}
...
Static survey written to: /tmp/.../replicate_survey.html (184.6 KB)
Report written to: /tmp/.../replicate_results.html (62.3 KB)
...
R version 4.6.0 (2025-04-11)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
:::

## Get started

```r
# Install from CRAN (after 0.3.2 is accepted)
install.packages("surveyframe")

# Install the development version from GitHub
remotes::install_github("MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe")

# Start immediately with the guided demo
library(surveyframe)
demo("survey", package = "surveyframe")

# Or open the builder with a preloaded demo instrument
launch_builder_demo()
```

::: {style="margin-top:1.2em;"}
**Documentation:** `browseVignettes("surveyframe")`
**Issues:** github.com/MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe/issues
**Paper:** *Journal of Statistical Software* — submission OJS 6454
:::
